title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government responds to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its approach to ensuring AI systems meet ethical, safety, and accountability standards. It details policies, regulatory measures, and collaborative frameworks aimed at fostering trustworthy AI while protecting public interests.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: This document outlines how Ofqual will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications, ensuring fairness, integrity, and transparency in testing and assessment. It was produced in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how AI systems use copyrighted materials and the legal and ethical impacts of this practice. It assesses the risks and proposes guidelines for responsible use of copyrighted content in AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has released a response to the House of Lords’ report on artificial intelligence, acknowledging the committee’s findings and the need for stronger oversight. It outlines plans to boost AI research, improve safety standards, and keep the UK competitive while protecting public interests.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the purpose, scope, and key questions for a committee reviewing how artificial intelligence interacts with public standards. It includes a list of frequently asked questions to guide the committee’s assessment and decision‑making.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on governance of artificial intelligence. The submission outlines CSPL's perspectives and recommendations on how AI should be governed.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy examines how artificial intelligence will shape rules and oversight for medical products, ensuring that new technologies meet safety and effectiveness standards. It outlines how the principles from the AI White Paper will be applied to create clearer, more adaptable regulations that balance innovation with patient protection.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the defence organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI user for its size. It focuses on responsible AI development and deployment to enhance decision‑making, operational efficiency, and national security.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan is a strategy from the Department for Transport that outlines how the government will partner with the transport industry to make the most of AI technologies. It also details measures to identify, assess, and manage any risks that could arise from using AI in transportation.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted material is being used to train and develop AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It summarizes progress to date, identifies challenges, and offers recommendations for balancing intellectual‑property rights with AI innovation.
